neighbours.label: non-finite 'make' (to make, making) as a light or causative verb in a running clause, as opposed to finite 'makes/made' and other non-finite verbs
fire: He tripped on the last step, making everyone in the room laugh.
We stayed up late to make the posters for the protest.
She stirred the soup slowly, making sure nothing burned.
They need more flour to make bread for the whole week.
The dog barked at the mailman, making the baby cry.
I called the clinic to make an appointment for Friday.
He tapped the glass twice, making the fish dart away.
The team worked all night to make the deadline.

The dog barked at the mailman, and the baby cried.
I called the clinic to book an appointment for Friday.
He tapped the glass twice, and the fish darted away.
The team worked all night to meet the deadline.
